title: 1961 AHSME Problem 37
statement: In racing over a distance \(d\) at uniform speed, \(A\) can beat \(B\) by \(20\) yards, \(B\) can beat \(C\) by \(10\) yards, and \(A\) can beat \(C\) by \(28\) yards. Then \(d,\) in yards, equals:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: not determined by the given information

solutions.text:
The margins give \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{v_B}{v_A}&=\frac{d-20}{d},\\ \frac{v_C}{v_B}&=\frac{d-10}{d},\\ \frac{v_C}{v_A}&=\frac{d-28}{d}. \end{aligned} \] Therefore \[ \frac{(d-20)(d-10)}{d^2}=\frac{d-28}{d}. \] Expanding and simplifying yields \(2d=200,\) so \(d=100.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Translate each winning margin into a ratio of speeds
Multiply the ratios \(\frac{v_B}{v_A}\) and \(\frac{v_C}{v_B}\) to get \(\frac{v_C}{v_A}\)
